en: For the gods, O Agni, ever seeking you with one mind, have sent you forward as their divine messenger; they have sent you forward with wisdom.

They have established the immortal among mortals for worship; they have brought forth the godly, the wise one; they have brought forth every godly, wise one. O Agni, turn toward your brother Varuṇa, toward the gods with your favor, toward those who delight in the sacrifice—the eldest of those who delight in the sacrifice.
The Aditya who upholds the cosmic order, the king who sustains the people—[I turn toward him].
O friend, turn toward your friend as a swift wheel [follows] a chariot, with speed, O wonder-worker, with speed for us!
O Agni, find favor with Varuna and with the Maruts who shine everywhere; O radiant one, grant well-being for our offspring and progeny; O wonder-worker, grant us well-being!
O Agni, you who are wise, may you ward off the wrath of the god Varuṇa from us. As the best of sacrificers, the most excellent bearer of oblations, and the radiant one, release us from all enmities.
O Agni, be our protector, our closest helper at the dawning of this very morning.

Worship Varuṇa for us, bestowing gifts; seek his favor, and be one who is easy for us to invoke. The sight of this most blessed god is most excellent among mortals, most wondrous to behold. Like the pure, heated ghee of the cow, it is desirable like the bounty of the divine milch-cow.
Threefold are those supreme, true, and desirable births of this divine Agni.
Enveloped within the infinite, he has come—pure, bright, noble, and shining intensely.
As the messenger, he desires all dwellings; he is the Hotṛ-priest with his golden chariot and his lovely tongue.
RV 4.1.8: With ruddy horses, beautiful, far-shining, ever-delightful like a banquet rich in food.
RV 4.1.9: He, the kinsman of sacrifice, makes men conscious; they lead him forward with a great cord.
He dwells in the dwellings of this mortal man, accomplishing his task; the god has attained the state of a sharer of wealth.
May that Agni, who knows the way, lead us toward the treasure allotted by the gods which belongs to him—
that which all the immortals fashioned through their wisdom, while Dyaus, the father and begetter, sprinkled the truth.
He was born first among the dwellings, at the base of the great [heavens], in the womb of this mid-air.
Footless and headless, he lay hidden, drawing away the boundaries in the lair of the bull.
The host first rose up, worthy of praise, in the womb of Truth, in the lair of the bull.
Longing, youthful, beautiful, and radiant—the seven dear ones brought him forth for the bull.
Here our human fathers sat down, aspiring toward the *ṛta*.
Invoking the dawns, they drove forth the cows from within the cave, which was a stone-fenced enclosure, easy to milk.
Having split the rock, they polished it; others proclaimed this deed of theirs from all sides.
Holding the reins of cattle, they sang their song of triumph; they found the light and yearned with their prayers.

With minds longing for kine, those eager men—with divine speech—opened the firm, obstructed mountain that held the cows, which stood encompassing the enclosure. They burst open the solid stall rich in cattle.

They conceived the first name of the cow; they found the thrice-seven highest names of the mother. Knowing that, the hosts of singers acclaimed her; the ruddy one became manifest through the glory of the cow.
The turbid darkness vanished; the sky shone forth; the radiance of the goddess Dawn has arisen.

Sūrya has mounted the vast field, beholding both the straight paths among mortals and the crooked ones. Then, awakening from behind, they have looked out; then indeed they have held fast the treasure allotted by heaven.
May all the gods in all their dwellings be present for our devotion; O Mitra and Varuṇa, let there be truth.
I would address the glowing Agni, the invoker, the sustainer of all, the most excellent sacrificer.
Like the pure udder of cows, he has been opened; like the purified juice of the stalk, he has been poured out.
He is the Aditi of all those worthy of sacrifice, the guest of all human beings.
May Agni Jātavedas, who wins the favor of the gods, be gracious to us.
He who is the immortal among mortals, the upholder of *ṛta*, the god established as the steward (*arati*) among the gods;
he, the Hotṛ, the most skilled in sacrifice, shall blaze with his greatness—Agni, whom men must impel with oblations.

O Son of Strength, born for us here today, you, O Agni, travel between both races as our messenger, having harnessed your lofty, straight-tailed stallions— both the bright and the white. I consider your two ruddy steeds, who increase your vigor and drip with clarity, to be swifter than thought, the very breath of the Eternal Order.
Yoking your two ruddy steeds, you move between you gods and the clans of mortals.

Bring hither Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Mitra among them, as well as Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and the Aśvins— O Agni, with your fine horses, good chariot, and noble gifts— to this people who offer excellent oblations.
O Agni, may this sacrifice be rich in cattle, rich in sheep, rich in horses, accompanied by heroic friends, and ever indestructible.
O Asura, may it be full of nourishment, rich in progeny, a long-lasting wealth with a broad foundation, and fit for the assembly.
He who, sweating, brings fuel to you, or heats his head out of devotion to you—

O Agni, as one who is self-strong by his own power, be its protector; guard it from every malevolent person. He who brings food to you, even though you have no need for it, and awakens the delightful guest while leaving some for himself— the seeker of gods who kindles you in his home—in him let there be lasting wealth, for he is a liberal giver.
He who praises you at evening or at dawn, or he who, possessing oblations, makes you dear—
like a swift horse in its own stall, rescue that worshipper from distress.
O Agni, he who offers to you, the immortal, and who performs service for you with uplifted ladle— him you protect.
RV 4.2.9: He who exerts himself shall not be deprived of wealth; no distress from the malevolent shall encompass him.

RV 4.2.10: O Agni, that mortal whose well-arranged sacrifice you, the god, accept with favor and grant gifts—may his priestly office be pleasing to you, O youngest one, and may we be the strengtheners of that worshiper.
May he, the wise one, distinguish between thought and thoughtlessness; like a charioteer on his back, may he separate the straight from the crooked among mortals.
O God, grant us wealth with noble offspring; bestow upon us freedom and protect us from bondage.
The undeceived sages have instructed the sage, establishing him as the guardian within the dwellings of the living.
From there, O Agni, may you behold these wondrous ones with your feet, visible through the movements of the noble one.

O Agni, youngest god, you who are a perfect guide for the priest who has pressed the soma and performs worship—bring wealth to the one who exerts himself, O impetuous one; bring broad, shining splendor for his protection, O filler of the people.

And now, O Agni, whatever we have done out of devotion to you with our feet, hands, and bodies— like those who fashion a chariot with their skillful work, the wise ones, seeking to win, have upheld the *ṛta*.
And so may we be born from the Mother Dawn as the seven sages, the first ordainers among men.

May we become the Aṅgirases, sons of Heaven; flaming, may we shatter the mountain rich in wealth. And as our ancient fathers of old, O Agni, who were aspiring toward *ṛta*, went toward the pure light, chanting their hymns; cleaving the earth, they uncovered the ruddy cows.
Performing good deeds, radiant, seeking the gods, they went forth like smiths blowing upon the births of metal, O Gods.

Purifying Agni and strengthening Indra, they approached, surrounding the wide stall of cattle. Like herds of cattle in a food-rich fold, he has beheld the generations of the Gods, O Mighty One, at their ultimate birth.

Even for mortals, the *urvaśīs* have yearned; for the increase of the noble one, of the future living man. We have worked for you with skillful hands; we have become [your servants]. The radiant dawns have dawned forth, spreading out the *ṛta*.
They have polished Agni, who is perfect in every way and most resplendent—the beautiful eye of the god.
RV_04.002.20.1 These hymns of praise we have recited for you, O Agni, the wise ordainer; as a seer, may you take pleasure in them.
RV_04.002.20.2 Blaze forth, shine brightly, and make us more prosperous; O you of many boons, bestow upon us great wealth.
RV_04.003.01.1 [I invoke] for you the King of the sacrifice, Rudra, the Hotṛ-priest of both worlds, whose worship is true.
Before the unperceived thunderbolt strikes, make Agni—whose form is like gold—your protector.
This is the seat we have prepared for you, as a longing, well-dressed wife [prepares] for her husband.
Enveloped and turned hitherward, sit down; these [fingers], O skillful one, are extended toward you.

O Ordainer, recite a hymn of praise to the immortal god who hears us, who is undaunted, who beholds men, and who is most gracious— him whom I, like a presser of Soma, laud as the one who extracts the honey. O Agni, you who perceive the Truth and are well-disposed, take heed of this our labor for the sake of this Truth.
When shall our hymns be shared in your banquet? When will our friendship be in your house?
How indeed, O Agni, will you report this to Varuṇa, how to Dyaus? What offense have we committed?
How will you speak to the bountiful Mitra, to Pṛthivī, to Aryaman, and to Bhaga?
When, O Agni, will you speak from the sacrificial hearths, you who grow strong; when to the powerful Vāta, who seeks splendor;
when to the Nāsatyas who travel around the earth? And what, O Agni, will you say to Rudra, the slayer of men?
How [will you speak] to the great Pūṣan, the bringer of nourishment; and how to Rudra, the liberal giver of oblations?
What would you say to Viṣṇu, the wide-striding, as seed? What, O Agni, to the lofty arrow? How would you answer when asked: "How [will you serve] the host of Maruts, the followers of Ṛta?
How the great Sun?"—thus to Aditi and the swift one, O Jātavedas, you who are wise, establish [the truth] from heaven.
By the *ṛta* the *ṛta* is established; I laud the cow, O Agni, together with her raw milk, the sweet cooked [milk].
Though she is black, she has swelled with bright nourishment, with the life-giving milk.
For by the *ṛta* indeed is the bull, the manly Agni, anointed with the milk of the back.
Moving without trembling, bestowing vital strength, the bull Pr̥śni milked the bright udder.
Splitting the mountain by means of the *ṛta*, the Aṅgirases shouted together with the cattle. The men sat around for prosperity at the breaking of dawn; the sun became manifest when Agni was born.
By the *ṛta*, O Agni, may the divine, immortal, and uninjured waters flow with their honeyed waves.
Like a prize-winning steed urged on in the races, let them ever hasten to flow forth.
May I never go to the sacrificial station of any one who deceives, nor of a neighbor who violates the law, nor of a kinsman.
O Agni, do not seek to recover the debt from a crooked brother; may we not suffer for the skill of a treacherous friend.
Protect us, O Agni, with your protections, you who are well-protected and pleased in battle;
O firm one, flash forth, shatter our narrow distress, and slay the *rakṣas*, even though it has grown very great.

O Agni, be well-disposed toward us through these hymns; O Hero, touch these strengths with our prayers. And, O Aṅgiras, accept our sacred formulations; may the praise, beloved by the gods, resound for you.
O Agni, Ordainer, all these secret ways and hidden words are for you who know them.
I have recited poetic hymns for the sage at the place of invocation, O inspired one, with my thoughts and songs of praise.
Display your power like a wide-spreading net; go forth like a mighty king with his host.
Rushing along your swift path, you are an archer; pierce the demons with your most scorching shafts.
Your whirling flames fly swiftly; following them, touch [the enemy] boldly, O glowing one.
O Agni, with your sacrificial ladle, cast forth your heats like winged insects; unbound, scatter your firebrands in every direction.
Dispatch your spies; be the swiftest one, an undeceivable guardian for this people.
RV 4.4.3: Whether he who plots evil against us be far away, O Agni, or near at hand—let no one provoke thy wrath.
RV 4.4.4.1: Rise up, O Agni! Spread yourself out against [the foe]! Burn down our enemies with your sharp weapon. 4.4.4.2:
O Kindled One, whoever has directed malice toward us, burn him down like dry brushwood.
Stand upright and pierce them; manifest thy divine powers against us, O Agni!
Slacken the firm bows of those impelled by demons; crush the enemies, whether they be kin or strangers.
He knows thy favor, O youngest one, he who has prepared a path for this prayerful hymn.
For him, may all days be auspicious; may he shine upon the doors of the enemy’s wealth and splendors.

Let that man, O Agni, be fortunate and a liberal giver who, throughout his own life, seeks to gratify you with constant oblations and hymns within his home. May every sacrifice for him result in auspicious days.
RV_04.004.08.1 I praise your benevolence; let the sound reach toward us. May this song of mine resound for you like a beloved wife.
RV_04.004.08.2 With fine horses and a splendid chariot, may we groom you. May you maintain our lordly powers day after day.
RV_04.004.09.1 May many a thing come here to you of its own accord, O illuminator of the darkness, as you shine day after day.
Playing and well-disposed, may we serve you, as we stand above the splendors of the people.
O Agni, he who approaches you with good horses and fine gold on a chariot laden with wealth—
of him you are the protector, of him the friend, provided he takes pleasure in offering hospitality to you in due order.

Through my kinship and with my words, I shatter the great [fortresses]. This [power] has come down to me from my father Gotama. O most youthful Hotṛ, of good will and domestic lord, take heed of this our speech. Born not of sleep, swift-acting, very gracious, unwearied, free from wolves, and most tireless.
RV 4.4.12.2: Let those protectors of thine, O Agni, sitting together in unison, guard us, O infallible one.
RV 4.4.13.1: Those protectors of thine, O Agni, who, seeing him, preserved the blind son of Mamatā from distress;
RV 4.4.13.2: The omniscient one protected those doers of good deeds; though the enemies sought to harm them, they did not succeed in harming them.
Through you may we be successful; protected by you, under your guidance, may we obtain spoils of war.
Accomplish both our prayers, O upholder of truth; act immediately, O one who is not to be shamed.
With this fuel, O Agni, may we worship you; accept the hymn of praise as it is being recited.
Burn the devouring demons; protect us from malice, from reproach, and from blame, O you who are great as Mitra! In harmony with the bounteous Vaiśvānara, how shall we offer great light to Agni?
With his perfect and lofty growth, he props himself up like a bank that supports a dam.
Do not revile him who, as a god, has bestowed this gift upon me, a mortal— Agni Vaiśvānara, the wise, the immortal, the discerning, the most manly, the mighty youth.
He is the Sāman of double strength, the great one with sharp points, the bull of a thousand seeds, the exceedingly powerful.
RV 4.5.3: Having discovered the track of the cow hidden away, Agni has declared his inspired thought to me.
RV 4.5.4: May Agni, the bounteous giver, consume with his most fervent flame those who violate the ordinances of Varuṇa and the beloved, steadfast laws of the mindful Mitra.
Like brotherless maidens wandering abroad, like women hostile to their husbands,
evil-minded, wicked, false, and untruthful, they have produced this deep place. O purifying Agni, upon me, who am so small and yet unyielding, you have placed this thought like a heavy burden.
You have boldly established the vast, profound, and mighty sevenfold back with sacrificial food.
May our purifying prayer, through its power of will, reach him who is truly one and common to all.
Upon the skin of the grass, on the summit of the beautiful dappled earth, the bright garment has been woven.
What of this speech of mine is to be proclaimed? They speak of that which is hidden in the secret cave.
When they have opened the enclosure of the ruddy cows like a gate, he guards the beloved tip of the form, the footstep of the bird.
And this indeed is the great face of the Great One, which the ancient cow, the ruddy one, has followed.
He has discovered him shining upon the station of *ṛta*, moving swiftly in secret, hastening on. Then, radiant, dwelling with his parents, he recognized the beautiful secret of *pṛśni*.
At the highest station of the Mother, near at hand, is the tongue of the Bull, of the outstretched flame.
I speak the truth with reverence when questioned, O Jātavedas, by your grace for whatever exists here.
You rule over all this: whatever wealth is in heaven and whatever treasure is upon the earth.
What portion of this wealth and what jewel shall be ours? Tell us, O wise Jātavedas.
RV 4.5.12.2: From the secret path, we have reached the highest point of this [world], yet like those who seek a lost track, we have not found its foundation.
RV 4.5.13.1: What are the boundaries and what are the guiding marks? How may we reach the desirable prize, like swift horses racing for the booty?
RV 4.5.13.2: When will the goddesses, the wives of the Immortal, extend over us with the splendor of the Sun, O Dawns?
With feeble, hollow, and deceptive speech, you have not satisfied us with your meager words.
And so, O Agni, what can those who are unarmed say here against you? Let them remain in their powerlessness.
The face of the bull, of this Vasu kindled for glory, has shone forth within the house.
Clad in brilliance, with a most beautiful form, he has shone like the earth with wealth—O Bountiful One, you who are desired by many.
Stand up erect for us, O Agni, Hotṛ-priest of the sacrifice, the best at worship among the gods.
For you indeed surpass every thought; you further the inspired wisdom even of the skilled sacrificer.
The unerring Hotṛ has been seated among the people, Agni, the delightful one, wise in the sacrificial assemblies.
Like the Sun, he has extended his radiant beam upward; like a pillar, he supports the smoke toward heaven.
Holding forth the well-blazing, gift-bearing, butter-dripping ladle, he moves to the right, choosing the host of gods.
The sacrificial post, newly born like a bull, well-placed and firmly fixed, anoints the victims.
Upon the strewn sacrificial grass, while the fire is kindled, the Adhvaryu priest stands upright, full of joy.
Agni, like a guardian of cattle or a Hotṛ-priest, goes around three times from of old, choosing his path.
Agni, the measured-stepper, goes around by himself, the Hotṛ-priest, delightful, sweet-voiced, and true to the *ṛta*.
His flames run like prize-winning horses; all beings are afraid when he has blazed forth.
O Agni, of beautiful countenance, auspicious is your appearance, lovely even though you are terrible and manifold.
RV 4.6.6.2: Your brilliance, which they do not obstruct with darkness, nor do the defilers bring any stain upon your body.
RV 4.6.7.1: Whose birth was not hindered by any obstacle, nor even by his mother and father when he sought it.
RV 4.6.7.2: Then Agni, the purifier, well-established like Mitra, has shone forth among the human clans.
Him, Agni, whom the five sisters dwelling together have brought forth twice over among the human tribes—
him who awakens at dawn, like a sharpened tooth, bright and fair-tongued, keen as an axe. These thy bay horses, O Agni, dripping with ghee, ruddy, straight-moving, and swift-moving.
The ruddy, bull-like, and straight-testicled wondrous ones have called upon the assembly of the gods.
Those flames of yours, O Agni, which move about— overpowering, unwearied, and brilliant—
are like hawks hastening to their goal, roaring loudly like the host of the Maruts.

RV 4.6.11.1: A prayer has been fashioned for you, O kindled one; let the priest recite the hymn; he sacrifices and distributes the portions. RV 4.6.11.2: Men have established Agni as the Hotṛ-priest; desiring his favor, they pay him homage, seeking the praise of the living. RV 4.7.1.1: This one has been established here as the first by the ordainers—the Hotṛ, most skilled in sacrifice, to be praised at the rites.
Whom Apnavāna and the Bhṛgus caused to shine forth—wondrous and pervasive among every tribe—in the woods;
O Agni, when shall there be for thee, the god, a continuous manifestation?
For then mortals have seized thee, who art to be praised among the people.
Beholding him, the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvān*), the wise one, as one beholds the sky with its stars;
him who brings laughter to all sacrifices in every house.
The swift messenger of Vivasvat, who moves toward all the peoples.
The Āyus have brought him, the banner, the Bhr̥gavāṇa, to every tribe.
They have established him as the Hotṛ priest in due order— the one who is conscious, the delightful one with purifying luster, the best of sacrificers through his seven stations.
Him, who has entered into his eternal mothers, who has taken refuge in the forest;
him who is wonderful, hidden in the cave, yet easy to find for one who seeks him anywhere.
When the gods rejoiced in the separation of the grain in that udder, in the abode of *ṛta*.
Great is Agni, to whom oblations are offered with reverence; the upholder of *ṛta* ever hastens toward the sacrifice.
Knowing the duties of the messenger for the sacrifice, and being fully aware of both ends of heaven and earth, you go as a messenger from of old, chosen and most wise, knowing the ascents of heaven.
Black is your path, O radiant one; your light shines before you; your moving flame is truly the wonder of wonders.
When she, yet unimpregnated, bears the germ, even as soon as born, you become a messenger.
As soon as he is born, his vigor is visible when the wind blows after his flame.
He brandishes his sharp tongue among the dry wood; he rends even solid foods apart with his jaws.

When he has carried away the food greedily with his greedy flame, the mighty Agni makes himself a greedy messenger. Consuming it, he follows the roar of the wind; like a swift horse, he is urged forward and incited.
I strive with my song for your messenger, the all-knowing, the immortal bearer of oblations, the most excellent sacrificer.
For he knows the treasury of wealth, the great ascent to heaven.
May he bring the gods here; he, the god, knows how to bend the gods to the one who follows the *ṛta* in his home;
he bestows even the most beloved treasures.
He is the Hotṛ; he, being wise, goes between [the worlds] on his mission as messenger, knowing the ascent to heaven.
May we be those who have honored Agni with offerings of oblations.
Those who, causing him to thrive, kindle him—
those have become renowned as winners of wealth and heroic power,
they who have offered worship unto Agni.
May riches desirable by many come to us day after day;
may strengths arise for us.
He is the inspired sage of the peoples, by his power over men.
He pierces like a swift arrow.
O Agni, have mercy; you are great, you who have come to this god-seeking people to sit upon the sacred grass.
He, the immortal, difficult to deceive among the human tribes, has become the messenger of all, a protector. He,
the joyous Hotṛ-priest, is led around the sacrificial seat during the rites of heaven.
And he sits down as the Potṛ priest; and Agni, the divine wife, at the sacrifice; and he sits down as the master of the house in the home; and he sits down as the Brahman priest.
For you go as the invoker of the people who perform the sacrifice,
and [you take] the oblations of men. You have indeed performed the office of messenger for him whose sacrifice you have enjoyed.
To carry the oblation of the mortal;
O Aṅgiras, find pleasure in our ritual, in our sacrifice,
and hear our invocation.
May your unassailable chariot reach us from every side— that chariot with which you protect those who offer oblations.
O Agni, today [we approach] that [sacrifice] with hymns, like a horse, like a blessed resolve that touches the heart.
May we prosper through your offerings.
For indeed, O Agni, you have become the charioteer of auspicious will, of skill, and of the effective truth.
Through these our hymns, O Agni, turn toward us; like the light of heaven, be present with all your gracious countenances.
Praising you today with these songs, O Agni, may we worship you.
Your powers thunder forth like those of heaven.
O Agni, your appearance is most sweet; even now by day, even now by night, it shines close at hand for glory, like a golden ornament.
Like clarified butter purified, thy body is stainless, pure like gold; that [body] of thine, O self-dependent one, shines like a golden ornament.
For even enmity, however committed, thou, O Agni, utterly drivest away from the mortal.
Thus from the sacrificer, O observer of *ṛta*.
May our friendships and brotherhoods with you gods be auspicious, O Agni; this is our kinship in this same dwelling, at this same udder.
O powerful Agni, auspicious is your countenance; it shines forth even near the sun.
Radiant to behold, it is seen even by night; in its form, food is visible, unblemished for the sight.
O Agni, born of many, being praised with fervor, disclose through your inspiration the thought for the singer, like the sky.
Whatever great thought you have bestowed, O radiant one, together with all the gods, grant that to us, O most mighty one.
From you, O Agni, are born poetic insights, from you come inspired thoughts, and from you arise hymns that bring success.
From you comes wealth adorned with heroes for the mortal who offers oblations and possesses such devotion.
From thee is born the vigorous steed, the bringer of booty, far-reaching, the fulfiller of desires, possessed of true strength;
from thee comes wealth impelled by the gods, bringing bliss; from thee, O Agni, comes the swift, speeding courser.
Thee, O Agni, the first god, the immortal one with the pleasant tongue, do mortal men seeking the gods worship.
They seek with their prayers the one who drives away hatred, the domestic friend, the lord of the house, the unerring.

Far from us you ward off lack of thought, far off misfortune, and far off every evil intent, when you protect us. O Agni, Son of Strength, you are auspicious at evening for him whom you, O God, accompany for his well-being.
O Agni, he who kindles you with the ladle uplifted, and prepares food for you thrice on this very day—
may he, being wise through your power, O Jātavedas, overcome his enemies with glorious splendors. He who, laboring with devotion, brings fuel to you, O Agni, honoring your great countenance—
Kindled at evening and at dawn, he prospers and dwells with wealth, striking down his enemies.
Agni is the lord of great dominion; Agni is the lord of booty and of supreme riches.
Most youthful and self-dependent, he bestows treasure upon the mortal who serves him in succession.
Whatever sin we have committed against you among men, O youngest one, through lack of thought or by any negligence—make us sinless before Aditi; loosen our offenses on every side, O Agni.
Even from great sin, O Agni, and from the presence of gods and mortals alike, deliver us from the wide expanse.

May we, your friends, never suffer harm; grant well-being and security to our children and descendants. Just as you, O Vasus, worthy of worship, once released even the Gaurī cow that was bound by the foot, so now release us from this distress; O Agni, prolong our life further.
Agni has looked upon the vanguard of the dawns as they shine forth, well-disposed toward the bestowing of treasures.
O Aśvins, come to the dwelling of the pious man; the god Sūrya rises up with his light.
The god Savitṛ has sent his radiance upward, shaking his banner like a warrior seeking cattle.

Varuṇa and Mitra follow their decree when they cause the Sun to ascend in heaven. Him whom they made for the dispersal of darkness— those who abide in firm security and do not seek rest for their own ends—
that Sun, the observer of all the moving world, the seven swift bay mares carry forward.
With your most swift steeds, you go weaving the thread, O God, spreading out the black garment. The rays of Sūrya, violently shaking, have cast away the darkness within the waters like a skin.
Not led by another, not bound, how is it that this one falls down face-down and then face-up?
By what inherent power does he come? Who has seen him? As the pillar of heaven, he stands firm and protects the vault of the sky.
Agni Jātavedas, the god, has looked out toward the Dawns as they shine with their splendors. O Nāsatyas, you of wide stride, come hither to this sacrifice of ours on your chariot.
The god Savitṛ has raised his banner aloft, creating light for the entire world. Sūrya has filled heaven, earth, and the mid-air, shining brightly with his rays.
The ruddy ones have come hither with light; great and wonderful, they shine brightly with their rays.
Awakening us for our welfare, the goddess Dawn approaches on her well-yoked chariot.
May those most excellent chariots and horses bring you both here at the breaking of dawn. For these Soma juices are for your drinking; O Bulls, rejoice at this sacrifice.
Unrestrained and unbound, how is it that this one does not fall down, face downward or face upward? Agni, our Hotṛ at the sacrifice, being a prize-winner, is led around,
the god worthy of worship among the gods.
Agni goes around the threefold sacrifice like a charioteer,
bestowing nourishment upon the gods.
The sage Agni, lord of booty, has stepped around the oblations.
Bestowing treasures upon the donor—
this [Agni] who is kindled for Sṛñjaya, the son of Devavāta,
is radiant and the subduer of enemies.
May a mortal man indeed have power over this such Agni, the sharp-toothed and bountiful. Him,
like a prize-winning steed, like the ruddy child of heaven—
Day after day they are cleansed. When the prince Sāhadevya awakened me with his two bay horses,
he came toward me like one summoned.
And those two adorable bay horses, I immediately accepted as a gift from the prince Sāhadevya.
O divine Aśvins, this is the prince Sāhadevya for you both.
May Somaka be long-lived.
O divine Aśvins, you two make that prince Sāhadevya long-lived.
Let the true Maghavan, the drinker of the dregs, come hither; let his bay steeds run toward us.
For him we have pressed this most potent juice; being praised, may he find his way here. O Hero, descend like one at the end of a journey, to gladden yourself today at this our libation.

Like Uśanas, the wise priest shall proclaim the hymn; he shall offer a prayer to the conscious Asura. Like a sage, accomplishing the secret rites, the bull shall sing, swelling with his outpouring. Thus from heaven he brought forth the seven singers; praising him, they have established the ordinances even by day.
When the beautiful light of heaven was found through hymns, they caused the great radiance to shine at the break of day;
the most heroic one, in his desire to help men, made the blinding darkness visible.
Indra, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, has grown to immeasurable power; with his greatness, he has filled both worlds.
Even beyond this, his greatness extends, he who has surpassed all worlds.
The mighty one, knowing all manly deeds, released the waters with his longing friends.
They who by their words even split the rock, the *uśij* opened the stall filled with cattle.

You struck down Vṛtra who had encompassed the waters; the earth, in accord with you, favored your thunderbolt. You sent forth the oceanic floods, O hero, bold one, becoming their lord through your might.
When you, O much-invoked one, shattered the rock for the waters, Saramā appeared before you.
As our leader, may you strike out abundant booty for us, shattering the cow-pens while being praised by the Aṅgirases.

O Maghavan, you whose mind is set on manly deeds, come toward the sage who calls upon you for aid in the winning of light; hasten to him with your protections when he invokes you for glory. Let the guileful Dasyu, devoid of prayer, perish.
Come home with a mind intent on slaying the Dasyus; let Kutsa be eager for your friendship.
Sit down in your own place, you two of like form; indeed, the woman who knows the *ṛta* shall distinguish between you two.
Seeking aid, you go in the same chariot with Kutsa, O impeller, as the master of the two bay steeds of Vāta.
Desiring to win booty like a prize to be seized, may the Seer, when he has struck, be ready for the decisive day.
For Kutsa, you struck down the insatiable Śuṣṇa; at the onset of the day, you crushed Kuyava and his thousands.
Instantly destroy the Dasyus with the help of Kutsa, and seize the wheel of the Sun in the encounter.
You delivered Pipru, who was swelling with might like a wild beast, into the hands of R̥jiśvan, the son of Vidathin.
You cast down fifty thousand black ones; you shattered his fortresses as old age consumes a garment.
When you, O Sūrya, placed your body near [the earth], your immortal form became manifest.
Like a wild elephant putting on his strength, like a terrifying lion bearing his weapons;

to Indra have desires come seeking wealth, longing for the libation as if for the winning of light. Seeking glory, exerting themselves with hymns, they are like a delightful home, like fair and nourishing prosperity.

We invoke that very Indra of yours, easy to call upon, who has performed many heroic deeds; he who, possessing desirable wealth, swiftly brings booty to a singer like me, even booty that must be won through struggle. When the sharp bolt falls among the people, O Hero, in whatever moment of conflict, [be our protector].
When the terrible encounter with the enemy occurs, then indeed be the protector of our bodies.
Be the helper of Vāmadeva’s inspired thoughts; be a friend, free from malice, in the winning of booty.
We have come to you for your providence; may you always be one of wide renown to the singer.
With these men who seek you, O Indra, with these liberal patrons, O Maghavan, in every battle—
surpassing our enemies with splendors like the heavens— we would rejoice through many nights and autumns.
Thus have we fashioned a prayer for Indra, the bull, the strong one, as the Bhr̥gus fashion a chariot.
RV 4.16.20: May our friendship never be severed; may you be our fierce protector and guardian of our bodies.
RV 4.16.21: Now, O Indra, being praised and lauded, cause nourishment to swell for the singer like rivers;
a new prayer has been fashioned for you, O Lord of Bay Steeds. Through this wisdom, may we be masters of chariots and eternal victors.
Great art thou, O Indra; indeed, the earth and the heaven have acknowledged thy sovereign power with great magnificence.
Having slain Vṛtra with thy might, thou didst release the rivers that had been swallowed by the serpent.
At the birth of thy brilliance, the heaven trembled; the earth trembled from fear of thine own wrath.
The well-founded mountains roared; the deserts were moistened; the waters flowed forth.
Hurling the thunderbolt with might, displaying his power through his strength, he shattered the mountain.
Exulting, he slew Vṛtra with the thunderbolt; the waters, their bull slain, rushed forward with speed.
Your father Dyaus considered himself a true hero; the maker of Indra performed the most skillful work.

He who begot him—the one with the thundering voice and the good thunderbolt—made him immovable from his seat, like the earth from its foundation. He alone causes the world to tremble; Indra, the much-invoked king of the peoples.
All rejoice in him in truth, at the gift of this generous god who is praised. Truly, all the Soma juices have become his; truly, the most intoxicating draughts belong to the great one.
Truly, you became the lord of treasures; O Indra, you have placed all the peoples under your gift.
Then, O Indra, as soon as you were born, you established all these peoples in their places.
O Maghavan, with your thunderbolt, you tore apart the dragon who lay across the flowing waters.
The ever-conquering, bold, and powerful Indra—the great, boundless bull armed with the excellent thunderbolt—[we invoke].
RV 4.17.8: He who is the slayer of Vṛtra and the winner of booty, the Maghavan who bestows riches and is most bountiful;
RV 4.17.9: He drives away the gathered hosts when he alone is heard of as the Maghavan in battles;
he brings the prize that he wins, and may we be dear to him in his friendship.
He is heard of as conquering and slaying; he also wins cattle in battle.
When Indra makes his wrath true, everything that is firm and everything that moves fears him.
Indra has won all the cattle, all the gold, and all the horses—the bounteous Maghavan who has conquered many.
With these men, he, the most heroic, is the distributor of wealth and the gatherer of riches by his powers.
How much does Indra regard his mother? How much his father, the progenitor who begot him?
He who, like the wind driven by swift-moving clouds that thunder, stirs up his own impetuous strength.
He makes the settled man unsettled; the Bounteous Lord raises up the dust in a whirlwind.
Shattering like heaven armed with lightning, the Bounteous Lord shall bestow wealth upon his praiser.
He has urged on the wheel of the sun and brought Etaśa to a halt as he was speeding along.
The black one, moving crookedly, sprinkles [the oblation] at the base of the skin, in the womb of this *rajas*.
Like a sacrificing priest at the dark [altar], he stands upon the black [earth].
Desiring cattle, seeking horses, and striving for strength, the inspired singers approach Indra, the bull, for friendship.
Seeking a wife, we cause the giver of wives—who possesses inexhaustible nourishment—to come forth, as one draws a water-jar from a well.

Be our protector when you are beheld, our kinsman, our overseer, and the comforter of those who offer Soma. As a friend, a father, and the most fatherly of fathers, create wide space for us who long for it, bestowing vital strength.
Be the protector of those who seek your friendship; as a friend, O Indra, being praised, bestow vital strength upon the one who lauds you.
For we have indeed performed service for you with zeal, magnifying you, O Indra, with these holy rites.
Praised is Indra, the Bountiful One, since he alone slays many irresistible Vṛtras.
RV 4.17.19.2: His singer is beloved, he under whose protection neither gods nor mortals can obstruct him.
RV 4.17.20.1: Thus may Indra, the bountiful and exuberant, the upholder of the people and the foeless one, make our prayers true.
RV 4.17.20.2: You are the king of all beings by birth; bestow upon us, the singer, great and glorious renown.

Now, O Indra, being praised and now being lauded, cause nourishment to swell for the singer like rivers. A new prayer has been fashioned for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds; through our devotion, may we be chariot-borne victors forever.
This is the well-trodden, ancient path by which all the gods were born.

From this very place let him be born fully grown; let him not cause his mother to fall away by that [wrong] path. I have not gone out from there; this is a difficult exit. I shall go out sideways, across the flanks.
Many things remain for me to do that have not yet been done. I will fight with one and consult with another.

He looked upon his departing mother and said: "I shall not go back; I will surely follow after. In the house of Tvaṣṭṛ, Indra drank the Soma pressed from a hundred vessels, the soma from the two ladles.
What could he accomplish by himself, whom she bore for a thousand months and many autumns?
Indeed, there is no counterpart to him among those already born, nor among those yet to be born.
Thinking him to be a reproach, his mother hid Indra within her secret place, suppressed by his own heroic power.
Then he arose, clothing himself in his own raiment; being born, he filled the two worlds, heaven and earth.
These waters flow forth, sounding *alala*, crying out together like the followers of Truth (*ṛtāvarī*).
Ask these [waters]: what is it that they are saying? Against what rock-bound enclosure do the waters break through?
What indeed do the waters say as their responses (*nivid*) to him? Do they intend to acknowledge Indra’s reproach?
RV 4.18.7: Having slain Vṛtra with his mighty weapon, my son released these rivers.
RV 4.18.8: Not for me did the young maiden abandon you; not for me did Kuṣavā swallow you.
Even the waters were gracious to my child; even Indra stood up for me with might.
O Maghavan, you struck down my own Vyansa, having pierced his jaws apart. Thus, being pierced, he became inferior; you crushed the head of the Dāsa with your weapon.
The young cow gave birth to the steadfast, invincible, and impetuous bull, Indra.
RV 4.18.10: The mother [let loose] the uncaressed calf for wandering, as he himself was seeking a path for his body.
RV 4.18.11: And the mother looked after the buffalo, saying, "O son, these gods are abandoning you.
Then Indra, about to slay Vṛtra, said, "O friend Viṣṇu, stride out yet more widely!"
Who made your mother a widow? Who sought to kill you as you were wandering?
What god was there to show you mercy when you seized your father by the foot and struck him down?
Out of malice I cooked the entrails of a dog; among the gods I found no one to comfort me.
I saw my wife being dishonored; then the falcon brought the honeyed mead to me.

Thus, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, all the gods here—those who are easily invoked and our protectors—choose you alone, the great, the exalted, the one who has grown vast, as their sole leader in the slaying of Vṛtra.
The gods released him like those worn out by age; O Indra, you became the sovereign ruler whose origin is truth.
You slew the serpent who lay encompassing the flood; you dug out the channels that nourish all things.
O Indra, [you struck] the one who was unsatiated, the wide-stretching, the unawakened, the one who did not wake, while he was deep in sleep.
With his thunderbolt, he split the serpent who lay across the seven downward-flowing rivers at their joints.
Indra, by his might, shook the earth to its foundation with his powers, as the wind stirs the waters;
longing for strength, he shattered the firm places and struck down the peaks of the mountains.
They have rushed forward like women toward their child; the pressing-stones have gone forth together like chariots.
You satisfied them as they spread out; you bound the waves and, O Indra, released the obstructed rivers.
You [released] the great, all-sustaining river flowing for Turvīti and Vayya.
He brought the waters to rest with homage; O Indra, you made the rivers easy to cross. Like surging billows, he caused the youthful, flowing streams—knowers of the *ṛta*—to swell;
he filled the parched deserts and plains. O Indra, you cast down the barren cows, the wives of the Dāsa, who were difficult to master.
Through many dawns and many celebrated autumns, having slain Vṛtra, he released the rivers.
Indra burst open the obstructed, tightly confined channels so that they might flow across the earth.
O Lord of the Bay Steeds, you brought forth from his dwelling the son of the unwedded woman, whom the ants had not given up.
Taking up the blind serpent, he saw clearly; the one who had been bound came forth, his joints were set together.
The wise man, knowing them, has proclaimed your ancient deeds to the learned, O King—how you have performed your manly, self-willed, and heroic acts.

Now, O Indra, being praised and glorified, cause nourishment to swell for the singer like rivers; a new prayer has been fashioned for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds. Through our devotion, may we be charioteers who ever win the prize.
May the fierce Indra come to us for our protection—from afar or from nearby—as the one who grants assistance.
With his most powerful [forces], the lord of men, thunderbolt in arm, victorious in the clash of battles over those who attack;

may Indra come toward us with his bay horses for our protection and for bounty. May the wielder of the thunderbolt, the generous and exuberant one, stand by this sacrifice of ours in the winning of the prize.
O Indra, placing this sacrifice of ours before you, you shall grant us our purpose.

O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, like a gambler winning wealth, may we through you conquer the enemy in battle. O self-dependent Lord, desiring it and well-disposed toward us, come now close to us for the well-pressed soma.
O Indra, drink of the offered honey; exhilarate yourself with the soma-juice that flows along the back of the altar.
I call toward Indra, the one invoked by many, who has overflowed with the new seers like a ripe tree or a victorious scythe-wielder; I call him as a young man, full of passion, calls upon a maiden.
Like a mountain, he who is self-strong and lofty is Indra; from of old he was born fierce for the sake of conquest.
Like a terrible wielder of the ancient thunderbolt, he is filled with wealth like a vessel brimming with water.
There is none indeed by birth who can resist him, nor is there anyone who can diminish his bounty or his great wealth.
Raining down thy fierce and mighty strength, O thou invoked by many, bestow wealth upon us.
I behold wealth and the dominion over the peoples; yea, thou art the one who opens the stall of the cattle. O helper of men, victorious in battles, thou leadest us toward a vast heap of riches.

By what power is he heard as the most powerful, by which the lofty one repeatedly performs his various deeds? He who best disperses distress for the liberal giver, then bestows wealth upon the singer.
Do not neglect us; bring it and give that to us—abundant wealth that you have to bestow upon the donor.
RV 4.20.10: For this new gift, for this praised hymn of yours, O Indra, we shall speak forth while offering our praise.

RV 4.20.11: Now, O Indra, being lauded and now being sung, cause nourishment to swell for the singer like rivers; a new prayer has been fashioned for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds. Through our devotion, may we be masters of chariots, ever victorious.
May Indra come to us for our protection; praised here, may the hero be our companion at the feast.
May he, whose many powers have increased, nourish his dominion like the sky, overwhelming all with his might.
Here, celebrate his manly deeds—the deeds of him who is of abundant splendor and great bounty—toward these men.
He whose will is like a sovereign in the assembly, who is victorious and a deliverer, prevails over the peoples.
May Indra come from heaven, from earth, swiftly from the ocean or from the watery realm;
may he come with the Maruts from the sun-maker’s place, or from afar from the seat of Cosmic Order, for our protection.
We shall praise that Indra in the assemblies, who rules over abundant and vast wealth—
Indra who conquers with Vāyu among the cattle-rich [herds], and who boldly leads us toward better fortune.
He who, establishing reverence upon reverence, raises his voice, generating it for the sake of sacrifice.

Striving forward with hymns, the Hotṛ priest should bring Indra hither to the sacrificial seats, he who possesses many boons. When those desiring the prayer hasten with devotion, sitting by the pressing-stone in the secret cave of Auśija—
[there comes] the invoker of the dwelling, the great bearer of oblations for us within the enclosures.

When the strength of the bull Bhārvara truly accompanies him for the singer’s gift; when he is in the secret place of Auśija, or when he is for the sake of prayer, for the journey, and for exhilaration. When he opens wide the expanses of the mountain, he quickens the swiftnesses of the waters with his milk.
RV 4.21.8.2: He has found the bull and the wild ox in their lair, when the wise ones bear him forth for the sake of strength.
RV 4.21.9.1: Auspicious are your hands, well-fashioned are your palms, O Indra, which bestow bounty upon the one who praises you.
RV 4.21.9.2: What is your dwelling? Why do you not exhilarate us? Why do you not rise up to gladden yourself with the gift to be given?
Thus indeed is Indra, the true sovereign, the slayer of Vṛtra; he has created wide space for the Pūru people.
O much-praised one, grant us wealth through your wisdom; may I partake of your divine favor. Now, O Indra, being lauded and praised, make nourishment swell for the singer like rivers.

RV 4.21.11: A new prayer has been fashioned for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds; through our devotion, may we be chariot-borne victors forever. RV 4.22.1: Whatever Indra has enjoyed and whatever he desires—that the Great and Mighty One shall surely accomplish for us.
RV 4.22.2: Maghavan, who goes forth bearing the stone by his might, accepts prayer, hymn, Soma, and songs of praise.

The bull, hurling his four-edged thunderbolt, the fierce, most manly, and powerful one, with his two arms— Wearing wool for the sake of glory, he has clothed himself in her for friendship, she whose joints [he has covered]. He who, being born as the most divine among gods, was great with mighty spoils and great impetuous strengths.
Wielding the eager thunderbolt in his arms, he made heaven and earth tremble with his might.
All the embankments and the many slopes shook, and at his lofty birth, heaven and earth quaked.
The mighty one brings together the two parents; like a bull among cattle, the winds roar as they move around him.

These indeed, O Indra, are your great deeds against the mighty, to be proclaimed at all the Soma-pressings— when you, O hero, bold one, acting with boldness and impetuous strength, struck the serpent with your thunderbolt.
All these true deeds of yours, O you of many manly powers, flow forth from the udder of the bull, even as the milch-cows stream forth.
Then indeed, O thou of virile mind, the rivers, fearing thee, rushed forth with speed.
There, O Lord of Bay Steeds, those divine sisters praised thee with their aids, O Indra,
when they were released by thee to flow along their long course after having been held back.
The exhilarating stalk has been pressed like a river; may the ritual effort and the power of the one who exerts himself come toward you.
May the twin rays of the glowing one, possessing great strength, come toward us like the swift rein of a bull.
O ever-conquering one, perform for us the highest and most excellent heroic deeds and powers of victory all at once.
RV_04.022.09.2 Make the Vṛtras easy for us to slay; strike down the weapon of the attacking mortal.
RV_04.022.10.1 Hear us well, O Indra; bestow upon us manifold spoils of war.
RV_04.022.10.2 Send forth all prosperities to us; O Maghavan, be a true giver of cattle to us.

Now, O Indra, being praised and extolled, cause nourishment to swell for the singer like rivers. A new prayer has been fashioned for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds; through our devotion, may we be charioteers who ever win the prize.
How has he grown great? Whose priest’s sacrifice does he favor as he approaches the Soma from the udder?
Drinking, desiring, and enjoying the soma-juice, the lofty one has grown strong for the sake of radiant wealth.
What hero has attained his shared feast? Who has partaken of him with his favors?
What of him is wondrous? How has he become known? And how has he become a helper for the growth of the striving worshiper?
How does Indra hear the oblation being offered? How, hearing it, does he know of our assistance?
What are his ancient praises? And how do they call him a fulfiller for the singer?
How may the one who exerts himself with devotion, meditating upon it, attain his wealth?
The god has become aware of my true words; may he, who has accepted our homage, graciously accept the sacrifice.
How, at the dawning of this very light of dawn, has the god taken pleasure in the friendship of a mortal?
How, and in what way, does he grant his friendship to those friends who have extended to him a well-yoked desire?
RV 4.23.6.1 What indeed is this vessel for friendship toward friends? When shall we proclaim your brotherhood?
RV 4.23.6.2 For the sake of glory, his forms are beautiful to behold; his outpourings are like the sun, most wonderful, providing nourishment from the cow.
RV 4.23.7.1 Seeking to destroy malice and the deceiver who lacks Indra, he sharpens his keen edges for the sake of impetuous assault.
RV 4.23.7.2: Where even debts are paid off like those who owe them, the fierce one has driven away the unknown dawns into the distance.
RV 4.23.8.1: For the strengthenings of *ṛta* are many; the thought of *ṛta* destroys crookedness.
RV 4.23.8.2: The song of *ṛta*, awakening and shining forth for the living man, has pierced the deaf ears.
The firm foundations of *ṛta* exist; manifold are its radiant beauties for the sake of wondrous form.
By means of *ṛta* they impel forth long-lasting nourishment; by means of *ṛta* the cows have entered into *ṛta*.
Holding fast to *ṛta*, one truly wins *ṛta*; the surge of *ṛta* is swift and seeks the cattle.
For the sake of *ṛta*, the two broad, vast, and deep worlds; for the sake of *ṛta*, the two supreme milch-cows yield their milk.
Now, O Indra, being praised and glorified, cause nourishment to swell for the singer like rivers.
A new prayer has been fashioned for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds; through this wisdom, may we be chariot-borne victors forever.
What excellent praise can turn Indra, the son of strength, toward us with his bounty?

For that hero, O people, is the giver of riches to the singer; he is the lord of cattle who bestows gifts upon us. He is to be invoked in the slaying of Vṛtra, he is to be praised—Indra, whose gifts are true and whose praises are well-sung.
On his journey, Maghavan bestows wide space upon the mortal who offers prayer, presses the Soma, and is devoted to him.

Him indeed the heroes call upon in the encounter; risking their own bodies, they make him their protector when both sides have come together for the mutual abandonment of life in the struggle to win offspring and progeny.
The people act with ritual zeal, striving together in their union, shouting to one another in the battle for waters.

When the warrior tribes have come together in conflict, then indeed some of them seek the favor of Indra in the encounter. Then indeed some worship the power of Indra; then let the cooked offering exceed the sacrificial cake.

Then indeed Soma shall separate those who have not pressed [the juice]; then indeed he shall take pleasure in sacrificing to the Bull. He creates wide space for him who thus presses Soma for Indra who desires it;
with a focused mind, undiverted, he makes that very person his friend in battles.
He who shall press Soma for Indra today, who shall cook the cooked offerings and roast the grains—
Indra, delighting in the hymns of that mindful one, shall bestow upon him virile strength.
When the impetuous one has distinguished the battle, when the noble one has looked toward the long contest.
The wife has called toward the bull, who is sharpened by the Soma-pressers within the dwelling.
He traded a greater price for a lesser one; having gone back, I regretted not selling.
He did not overvalue the lesser for the greater; those with feeble skill milk out the profit.

Who will buy this Indra of mine for ten milch-cows? When he has struck down the Vṛtras, let him give him back to me. Now, O Indra, being praised and lauded, make nourishment swell for the singer like rivers.
RV 4.24.11: A new prayer has been fashioned for you, O Lord of Bay Steeds; through this inspired thought, may we be chariot-warriors and ever-victorious.
RV 4.25.1: Who today, being a man devoted to the gods and desiring it, has taken pleasure in the friendship of Indra?
Or who, when the fire is kindled and the Soma is pressed, prays for great assistance on the decisive day?
Who has bowed with speech to the one worthy of Soma? Who becomes mindful as the dawns break?
Who desires Indra’s alliance, who his friendship, who his brotherhood? And who seeks aid for the sage? Who today chooses the protection of the gods? Who prays to the Ādityas and Aditi for light?
Whose pressed stalk of soma do the Aśvins, Indra, and Agni drink with a well-disposed mind?
To him may Agni Bhārata grant protection; may he long behold the sun rising.
He who says, "Let us press the juice for Indra," for the manly hero, the most heroic among men—
Neither many nor few overcome him; Aditi shall grant him wide protection.
Dear to Indra is the doer of good, dear the one who is mindful, dear the one who protects well, and dear is he who offers Soma.
This hero, the protector, the swift victor, makes the cooked offering his own alone when the Soma is pressed.
Among those who do not press the soma, there is no kinsman, no friend, and no relative; he is difficult to approach for the one who offers nothing and speaks no words of praise.
Indra, the drinker of the pressed juice, does not form an alliance with the wealthy Paṇi who does not press the soma.
He seizes his wealth and strikes him bare; he becomes the exclusive possessor for the one who presses the juice and prepares the cooked offering.
The highest, the lowest, and those in the middle call upon Indra; those traveling and those resting call upon Indra.
Those dwelling at peace and those fighting, men seeking booty, invoke Indra.
I was Manu and I was Sūrya; I am the seer Kakṣīvat, the inspired singer.
I have guided Kutsa, the son of Arjuni; I am the seer Uśanas—let him behold me! I gave the earth to the Ārya; I gave rain to the mortal who offers oblations.
I led forth the lowing waters; the gods followed my will.
Rejoicing, I shattered the ninety-nine fortresses of Śambara all at once;
the hundredth stronghold I gave up entirely when I protected Divodāsa Atithigva.
May that falcon be foremost among the falcons, O Maruts, for he is swift-flying.
When the fair-winged one, by his own inherent power, bore the god-pleasing oblation for Manu without wheels;
when he, trembling from there, was sent forth upon the broad, ruddy path swift as thought—
then the falcon went quickly with the honeyed Soma and won glory here.
The swift hawk, the bird, bringing the exhilarating draught from afar,
bearing the stalk while holding it fast, has brought the Soma that wins the gods, having taken it from yonder highest heaven.
Having taken it, the hawk has brought the Soma— ten thousand and a hundred pressings all at once.

RV 4.26.7.2: Here the wise one has abandoned the enemies in the exhilaration of Soma; the unerring one [has left behind] the foolish. RV 4.27.1.1: While still in the womb, I indeed recognized all these generations of the gods.
RV 4.27.1.2: A hundred iron fortresses guarded me; then, like a hawk, I flew forth with speed.
Truly, he did not carry me away against my will; through his skill and heroic power, he overcame him.
With a swift stride, the wise one abandoned the enemies and, growing strong, crossed over the winds.
When the falcon cried out from heaven, or when the winds bore the wise one away.
When Kr̥śānu, the archer, eager in his mind, loosed the swift-flying bowstring against him;
The Falcon bore him from the lofty ridge, as R̥jipyin bore Bhujyu for Indra’s sake. His feathered wing fell within his flight, as he sped along on the path of the bird.
RV_04.027.05.1 Then Maghavan [took] the white jar, anointed with milk, swelling with the bright juice;

RV_04.027.05.2 the first of the honeyed [draught], presented by the *adhvaryu*s—Indra took it for exhilaration, the Hero took it for exhilaration, that he might drink. RV_04.028.01.1 With thee as his ally, O Soma, through that friendship of thine, Indra caused the waters to flow for Manu. Who [could restrain him]?

He slew the serpent and set free the seven rivers; he threw open the channels that were as if closed up. O Indu, with you as his ally, Indra by force instantly struck down the wheel of the Sun as it rolled upon the high ridge; thus was the life of the great oppressor destroyed.
Indra slew them and Agni burnt them up, O Indu; before midday, in the encounter, he struck down the Dasyus.
With his arrow, he laid low many thousands of those who, like those going by their own will, were in difficult terrain and ill-housed dwellings.
Indra made the Dasyus lower than all, and he rendered the Dāsa clans unworthy of praise.
You two repelled them, you crushed the enemies, and you obtained recompense with your weapons.
Thus, O bounteous ones, that truth is yours both: Indra and Soma, you tore open the enclosure of horses and cattle, which was barred by a stone;
you released them, piercing even the earth itself.
O Indra, being praised, come to us with strengths and aids, exhilarated by the bay steeds;

passing even over the many libations of the enemy, you who are celebrated with hymns as one whose bounty is true. For he, the manly and wise one, comes indeed when invoked by the pressers to the sacrifice.
He who possesses fine horses, being fearless and confident, rejoices with his heroes along with those who have pressed the soma.
One should cause his ears to hear so that he may strive for booty and rejoice according to the beloved direction. Raining down wealth, the mighty Indra shall make for us good paths and security.
He who comes with aid to the one who implores him, to the inspired singer who thus calls upon him and praises him—
placing the swift steeds himself upon the yoke-poles, he whose arm wields the thunderbolt brings hundreds and thousands.
O Maghavan Indra, protected by you, may we be your wise patrons, singing your praises.
Having partaken of the wealth of the lofty heaven, which is rich in food and desirable for bestowing, [we have come] to its giving.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, there is none higher than you, nor any greater;
indeed, there is no one else like you.
Truly, all the peoples have turned to follow you, as wheels turn after the chariot.
Truly, you are renowned as great.
Even all the gods together could not prevail against you, O Indra.
When you made the days and nights longer; when,
for the sake of those who were oppressed, you stole away the sun from Kutsa as he fought.
Where you alone, O Indra, fought against all the impetuous gods, you struck down the attackers.
And where, for the sake of a mortal, O Indra, you caused the sun to flow forth.
With your powers you protected Etaśa.
And why, O Vṛtra-slayer, are you so exceedingly wrathful, O Maghavan? It was then that you overcame the Dānu.

And this indeed was the heroic deed, O Indra, the manly exploit you performed: that you slew the daughter of Heaven, she who was ill-disposed toward marriage. Even the daughter of Heaven, the great one being glorified—by the great [Indra]—you struck down.
O Indra, you crushed Uṣas.
Uṣas fled from the chariot, terrified of the crushed [remains].
When the bull struck her down.
This wagon of hers lies here, utterly crushed by the Vipāś;
she has fled far away into the distance. And she has crossed the Sindhu, which spreads wide over the earth.
Thou hast encompassed them, O Indra, by thy creative power;
and with boldness, thou didst seize the possession of Śuṣṇa when thou crushedst his fortresses.
And you struck down Śambara, the Dāsa son of Kulitara, from the lofty mountain, O Indra.
And you slew the hundreds of thousands belonging to the Dāsa Varcin.
He [placed him] above the five spokes as if upon wheels.
And Indra, the Lord of a Hundred Powers, caused that son of the unwedded woman who had been cast away to share in the hymns of praise.

And those two, Turvaśa and Yadu, who were not swimming, the Lord of Might, Indra, knowing [the way], brought across. And those two Āryas, O Indra, he brought instantly across to the far side of the Sarayu.
From the flood, you slew Citraratha.
You led away the two who had been abandoned, the blind and the lame, O slayer of Vṛtra;
that favor of yours is not to be attained [by others].
Indra shattered a hundred fortresses made of stone for the liberal Divodāsa. He sent thirty thousand to sleep with his blows for the sake of Dabhīti.
Indra, by his creative power (*māyā*), [overcame] the Dāsas.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, you alone are the common lord of cattle, you who have shaken all these things.
And now, O Indra, whatever manly deed you shall perform with your power—
may no one today diminish that. O attentive one, may the god Aryaman grant you every desirable thing.
May Pūṣan grant us what is desirable, may Bhaga grant what is desirable, and may the god Karūlatī grant what is desirable.
With what aid will the wondrous one, our ever-increasing friend, come to us? With what most powerful host?
RV_04.031.02.1 Which true one among the exhilarations, most bountiful, will intoxicate you with the soma-juice?
RV_04.031.02.2 So that you may break open even the firmest wealth.
RV_04.031.03.1 Come then as the protector of us, your friends and singers.
May you be ours with a hundred aids. Turn toward us as a wheel turns for a steed,
with the teams of the people.
For you come down the slope of our intentions, as if to your own station;
I have partaken together with Sūrya.
O Indra, when your wrathful powers and your wheels have sped forth together.
Now indeed in you, and now in Sūrya. And indeed they call you, O Lord of Might (*śacīpate*), Maghavan, the giver who does not hesitate.
And indeed, at once to the one who has labored and pressed the juice, you bestow abundant wealth. For not even a hundred obstructors can restrain your bounty.
He will not perform mighty deeds against us. May your hundred aids protect us, may your thousand succors protect us,
and may all your assistances be ours.
Choose us here for friendship and for well-being,
for great wealth that reaches to heaven. Favor us always, O Indra, with abundant riches.
With all your aids, [protect] us.
For us, open up those cow-filled enclosures like a hunter,
O Indra, with your newest aids.
O Indra, may our chariot, bold, resplendent, and unshakable, advance,
seeking cattle and seeking horses.
O Sūrya, among the gods, establish for us the highest glory.
Like the highest heaven above;
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, come quickly to our side with your great aids.
Even though you are swift and impetuous, O Wondrous One, you are among those who possess wondrous power;
you perform wonders for our protection.
Even with the few, you slay the more numerous and the mighty with your might.
Those who are with you, O Indra, together with their friends—we, O Indra, are with you; we sing our praise to you.
Protect each and every one of us!
O wielder of the stone, come to us with your wondrous, blameless, and invincible aids. O Indra, may we truly become the friends of one such as you, who possesses cattle.
Yoke [the horses] for the eager prize!
For you alone, O Indra, rule over the prize consisting of cattle; therefore, grant us great nourishment.
RV 4.32.8: No one can turn you away from what you wish to give as wealth when you are praised, O Indra, lover of songs, for the sake of those who laud you.
RV 4.32.9: The Gotamas have celebrated you with their song, that you may grant them gifts.
O Indra, for the sake of impetuous strength! We shall proclaim your heroic deeds, those which you, exhilarated by the soma, performed by attacking and shattering the fortresses of the Dāsas.

The wise ones sing those manly deeds which you have performed for them, O Indra, lover of songs, when the soma juices are pressed. The Gotamas, who bring hymns of praise, have increased your strength, O Indra.
Bestow upon them glory accompanied by heroic sons.
For since you, O Indra, are the common possessor of all people,
we invoke you.
O Vasu, turn toward us;
rejoice well in our soma-juice, O Indra, drinker of soma, from these our libations. May the hymn of our thoughts reach you, O Indra.
Turn your two bay steeds hitherward; eat our sacrificial cake and take pleasure in our songs,
as a suitor takes pleasure in a young woman.
We implore Indra for a thousand harnessed stallions;
a hundred jars of Soma.
We cause a thousand and a hundred of your cattle to flow toward us.
May your bounty come to us from here.
We have received ten golden jars from you;
you are a great giver, O slayer of Vṛtra.
O bountiful giver, give us much; let not little come to us, but bring much hither!
For indeed, O Indra, you desire to give much. For you are renowned in many places as a bountiful giver, O hero, slayer of Vṛtra.
Grant us a share in your bounty. O far-seeing one, grandson of the winner of cattle, I praise your two tawny steeds; do not let them hold back the cows.
Like two young girls, uncovered, upon a new wooden seat, small and brown, they shine resplendent during their journeys.
They are ready for me at the coming of dawn, and ready at the departure of the night.
The two brown ones, unfailing on their journeys.

Send forth your voice like a messenger to the *Ṛbhus*; I praise the white cow Śvaitarī to provide a sacrificial strew for them—those who, impelled by the wind, with their swift movements, have in an instant become active throughout the sky.
When the Ṛbhus performed service for their parents with skillful deeds and wondrous powers,
then those wise ones attained the friendship of the gods and brought prosperity to their thought.
They who made their parents young again, who had lain decrepit like old posts at the sacrificial stake.
May they— Vāja, Vibhvan, and Ṛbhu, accompanied by Indra and possessing sweet draughts—
protect our sacrifice. Since for a year the Ṛbhus guarded the cow, since for a year the Ṛbhus fashioned the skin,
and since for a year they carried its parts, through those labors they attained immortality.
The eldest said, "Make two cups," the younger said, "Let us make three," and the youngest said, "Let us make four. Tvaṣṭṛ was amazed at these words of yours, O Ṛbhus.
The heroes spoke the truth, for so indeed they did; the Ṛbhus followed this their own inherent power.
Tvaṣṭṛ, having beheld them, looked upon the four shining chalices as if they were the gods themselves.
When the Ṛbhus, rejoicing and resting in the hospitality of Agohya for twelve days,
they made the fields fertile, led forth the rivers, established plants in the desert, and brought the waters to the lowlands.
RV_04.033.08.1 Those who fashioned the well-rolling chariot that carries heroes, and the cow who quickens all and assumes every form;
RV_04.033.08.2 May those Ṛbhus fashion wealth for us—they who possess their own splendor, who are skillful in work, and deft of hand.
RV_04.033.09.1 For the gods indeed took pleasure in their labor, contemplating it with wisdom and with their minds.

Vāja became the skillful artisan of the gods; Ṛbhukṣan was that of Indra, and Vibhvan of Varuṇa. Those who, rejoicing with wisdom and hymns, fashioned for Indra the two bay steeds so well-yoked—O Ṛbhus, bestowing prosperity upon us, grant us increase of wealth and treasures like friends seeking security.

This day they have assigned for you the drinking of the soma and exhilaration; O gods, it is not without toil that one attains friendship with you. O Rbhus, bestow treasures upon us now at this third libation.
O Rbhu, Vibhvan, Vaja, and Indra, come to this sacrifice of ours to grant us jewels.
For now indeed the goddess Dhiṣaṇā has ordained your drinking at these days; your exhilarations have come together.
Knowing your birth, O Ṛbhus, you whose treasure is booty—rejoice with the seasons!
Your exhilarations have come together, as has your inspired wisdom; send forth to us wealth accompanied by noble heroes.
RV 4.34.3.1 This sacrifice has been prepared for you, O Ṛbhus, which you have accepted as you did from Manu since days of old.
RV 4.34.3.2 Delighted, they have turned toward you; all of you, O Vājas, have become foremost.
RV 4.34.4.1 Now, O heroes, the granting of treasure has come to the mortal who serves you and offers oblations.
Drink, O Vājas and Ṛbhus; the great third libation has been offered to you for exhilaration. Come hither, O Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, you mighty heroes who are praised, bringing us great wealth.
These draughts have come to you at the close of days, as cows go to their stall.
O sons of strength, come hither to this sacrifice, being invoked with reverence!
O wise ones, being of one accord, drink of this mead for which you are present, as givers of treasures, accompanied by Indra.
O Indra, lover of songs, drink the Soma in harmony with Varuṇa; drink it in harmony with the Maruts.
In harmony with the *agnipās* (those who drink first) and the *ṛtupās* (those who drink at the proper seasons), in harmony with the *gnās* (the divine wives) who bestow treasures;
In harmony with the Ādityas, rejoice; in harmony with the mountains, O Ṛbhus;
In harmony with the divine Savitṛ, in harmony with the rivers that bestow treasures.

The *Ṛbhus* who [strengthened] the Aśvins, who [strengthened] their parents, and who by their aid fashioned the milch-cow and the horses; the *Ṛbhus* who [fashioned] the armor, who [separated] the two worlds apart, and who, being far-reaching heroes, performed noble deeds.
You who bestow wealth consisting of cattle, of booty, of brave sons, of treasures, and of abundant food.
O *Ṛbhus*, you who drink first and are exhilarated, bestow [wealth] upon us and upon those who praise your gift.
You have not been absent; we have not let you thirst at this sacrifice, O *Ṛbhus*. You have not been left without praise.
Rejoice with Indra, with the Maruts, and with the kings, O gods, for the granting of treasures.
Come here, O sons of strength, O R̥bhus, sons of Sudhanvan; do not stay away.
For at this libation of yours is the bestowing of treasures; may your exhilarations follow after Indra.
The bestowing of treasures by the R̥bhus has arrived here; there has been the drinking of the well-pressed Soma.
When, through skillful action and through your own dexterity, you fashioned the single chalice into four;
when you divided the chalice into four parts, O friend, you said, "Teach us how.
Then, O Vājas, you R̥bhus with your skillful hands reached the path of immortality, the assembly of the gods.
Of what material was this cup that you fashioned into four by your poetic wisdom? Now press the juice for the exhilaration of the libation; drink, O Ṛbhus, of the honeyed Soma.
By your skillful power you made your parents young again; by your skillful power you fashioned the cup for the drinking of the gods.

With skillful power, O Ṛbhus, you fashioned the two bay steeds, the winners of wealth, the carriers of Indra, you who possess the treasure of booty. O Vājas, for him who presses the sharp libation for your exhilaration at the close of days,
O Ṛbhus— ye mighty ones, being exhilarated, fashion for him wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
O Lord of the tawny steeds, you drank the pressed juice at dawn; the midday libation is yours alone.
Drink now together with the Ṛbhus, the bestowers of jewels, whom you, O Indra, have made your friends through their skillful deeds.
Those gods who became [manifest] through their skillful deeds have settled upon heaven like falcons.
Bestow wealth upon us, O sons of strength; you, the sons of Sudhanvan, have become immortal.
When you, with skillful hands and noble works, created the third libation as a bestowal of treasure, then, O Ṛbhus, drink this poured offering together with your exhilarating powers of Indra.
Born without horses and without reins, the praiseworthy three-wheeled chariot rolls around the firmament.
O Ṛbhus, that proclamation of your divine power is great, in that you nourish both heaven and earth.
Those wise ones who, through meditation upon their thought, fashioned the well-rolling chariot that does not swerve.

RV 4.36.2: We now announce this [offering] to you, O Vājas and Ṛbhus, for the drinking of this libation. RV 4.36.3: That greatness of yours, O Vājas and Ṛbhus, has become well-proclaimed among the gods, O Vibhūs, since you fashioned the aged parents—who were worn out by old age—into young men again so that they might move about.
RV 4.36.4.1: You made the single chalice fourfold; by your inspired thoughts, you brought forth the cow from the hide.
4.2: Then you attained immortality among the gods; O Vājas and Ṛbhus, that deed of yours is worthy of praise.
RV 4.36.5.1: From the Ṛbhus comes wealth most renowned, which the heroes, famed for their vigor, have generated.
Fashioned by Vibhvan, he is to be proclaimed at the assemblies—he whom you, O gods, protect; he is the one who observes all people.

He is the prize-winning steed, he is the seer through his eloquence, he is the hero, the archer invincible in battles. He possesses abundance of wealth and heroic strength—he whom Vāja, Vibhvan, and the Ṛbhus have aided.
The most excellent and beautiful ornament has been placed upon you; O Vājas and Ṛbhus, take pleasure in this hymn of praise.
For you are wise seers, possessed of inspired insight; as such, we make ourselves known to you with this sacred prayer (*brahman*).
From your wisdoms (*dhiṣaṇā*), you who are all-knowing, [bestow] upon us all the enjoyments that are beneficial to men.
Bestow upon us resplendent strength, most excellent and bull-like in vigor; O Ṛbhus, fashion for us wealth and vital force.

Bestowing here offspring and here riches, fashion for us here a fame accompanied by heroic sons— that brilliant strength, O Ṛbhus, by which we may distinguish ourselves above others; grant that to us.

O Vājas, Ṛbhukṣans, and gods, come to our sacrifice by the paths traveled by the gods, just as you accept the sacrifice among these human clans, O joyous ones, on the auspicious days of the year. May these sacrifices be pleasing to your hearts and minds; may they today go forth, clothed in ghee, as offerings well-accepted.
RV_04.037.02.2 Forward for you the pressed juices, full, hasten; having been drunk, they exhilarate for wisdom and skill.

RV_04.037.03.1 Just as the threefold gift ordained by the gods has been bestowed upon you, O Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, so has this hymn been offered to you. I offer Soma among the later clans, as Manus did, together with you who dwell in the high heavens.
For you have become possessors of fat horses and radiant chariots, with iron helmets, powerful, and adorned with fine golden ornaments.
O sons of Indra, O grandsons of strength, may this foremost [draught] be noticed by you for exhilaration.
O R̥bhukṣans, [bring] the wealth of R̥bhu, the most victorious companion in the contest for booty.
We invoke him who is accompanied by Indra, the most bountiful winner of wealth, who possesses the Aśvins. O Ṛbhus, that mortal whom you and Indra protect—
may he be a winner through his inspired thoughts at the winning of the prize, and with his steed.
O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣans, find out the paths for us to sacrifice;
O wise ones, being praised, may you enable us to cross over all directions.
O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣans, O Indra, O Nāsatyas, grant that wealth to us.
Bring together the horse for the people; O Puru, bestow it abundantly for the granting of wealth.
For indeed, yours are those ancient gifts which Trasadasyu bestowed upon the Pūrus as he released them.
You two gave [them] the winners of fields, the winners of fertile lands, and a fierce, overwhelming blow against the Dasyus.
And you two have bestowed upon us Dadhikrā, the prize-winner, who overcomes many, and who belongs to all people;
swift as a soaring hawk, dappled, rapid, worthy of praise, like a brave king and lord of men.
