All the Pūrus rejoice with delight as he rushes forth like one speeding down a steep descent.

Like a hero eager for wisdom, he seizes with his feet; like the wind, he rushes along, overtaking the chariot. He who, holding back the prize-winning [booty] in battles, moves forward as a conqueror, going among the cattle.
Manifestly straight, observing the sacrificial assemblies, he has passed beyond the obstructer, encompassing the waters of the living man.
And indeed, the people cry out after him in battles as if after a thief who has stolen a garment—
him who, though appearing lowly, is like a swift falcon, hastening toward glory and toward a herd of cattle.
And indeed, among us, he who is about to race forward first urges on his chariots in rows.
Like a handsome suitor preparing his garland, licking up the dust as he displays his brilliance;
and that vigorous, victorious steed, faithful to the *ṛta*, listening with his whole body in the assembly of battle—
speeding among those who hasten, straight-flying and striving, he scatters the dust over his brows.
And indeed, at his roar, as if from the sky, men tremble before him when he is wrathful and attacking.
When he has fought against a thousand, he becomes irresistible, terrible in his onset.
And indeed, people praise his speed, the overwhelming power of the swift one who wins over the peoples.
And of him they say, as they disperse in the encounter: "Dadhikrā has sped away with thousands.
Dadhikrā, by his might, has overspread the five peoples, as the sun with its light spreads over the waters.
May the prize-winning steed, winner of thousands and hundreds, fill these my words with sweetness.
We shall now praise the swift Dadhikrā; let us celebrate him who belongs to heaven and earth.
May the dawning Dawns inspire me and carry me across all difficulties.
I celebrate the great steed Dadhikrāvan, the filler of the mind, the bull of many boons.
RV 4.39.2: That radiant Agni, the conqueror, whom you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, bestowed upon the Pūrus;
RV 4.39.3: May Aditi make him sinless—he who has offered praise for the horse Dadhikrāvan when the fire is kindled at the breaking of dawn—being in harmony with both Mitra and Varuṇa.
We have meditated upon the food and strength of the great Dadhikrāvan, the auspicious name of the Maruts.
For our well-being, we invoke Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, and Indra, whose arm wields the thunderbolt. Both [classes of gods], rising up and approaching the sacrifice, call upon him as they do Indra.
RV_04.039.05.2 O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two have granted us Dadhikrā, the swift steed, as a benefactor for mortal man.
RV_04.039.06.1 I have celebrated Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, the spirited horse.
May he make our mouths fragrant; may he prolong our lives.
Let us now celebrate Dadhikrāvan; may all the Dawns inspire me.
[May they inspire me] with the waters, Agni, the Dawn, Sūrya, and Bṛhaspati, the victorious son of Aṅgiras.
The warrior, seeking booty, seeking cattle, worthy of praise, shall hasten toward the nourishment of the Dawns for the sake of glory.
The true, swift, and gliding Dadhikrāvan, flying like a bird, has generated food, vigor, and light.
And indeed, as he runs and hastens, the wind blows after him like the wing of a bird eager for its prey;
as Dadhikrāvan speeds along with his might, like a swooping falcon around the bend.
And this vigorous steed, bound by the neck, at the flanks, and in the mouth, hastens toward the whip. Dadhikrā, having exerted his strength, has leaped along the curves of the paths.
The swan dwelling in purity, the Vasu dwelling in the mid-air, the Hotṛ dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house.
RV 4.40.5: Seated among men, seated in the best of places, seated in the *ṛta*, seated in the sky; born of the waters, born of the kine, born of the *ṛta*, born of the mountains—the *ṛta* itself.
RV 4.41.1: O Indra and Varuṇa, what praise-offering accompanied by oblations has reached you for favor, like the immortal Hotṛ-priest?
RV 4.41.2: O Indra and Varuṇa, may that prayer, full of wisdom and uttered by us, which touches your hearts, be accepted with reverence.

The mortal who, providing offerings, has made Indra and Varuṇa his two divine allies for friendship—he slays the Vṛtras and his enemies in battles; or through their great protections, he becomes renowned. Indra and Varuṇa are indeed most liberal in bestowing treasure upon men who labor with devotion. Thus, O gods, do you grant wealth to those who strive.

If you two, as friends for the sake of friendship, delight yourselves with the pressed Soma juices and abundant nourishment— O Indra and Varuṇa, you two fierce ones, hurl your most powerful missile, the thunderbolt,
against him who is evil toward us, the wolfish Dabhīti; measure out your overwhelming power upon him.
O Indra and Varuṇa, be the lovers of this prayer, like two bulls of a cow.
May she yield for us like a great cow who has gone to pasture, with milk in a thousand streams.
For the sake of our children and progeny, for fertile fields, for the sight of the sun, and for manly strength, O heroes.

RV_04.041.06.2 May Indra and Varuṇa be with us here with their protections, O wonder-workers, in the decisive struggle. RV_04.041.07.1 For it is you two, the abundant ones, whom we choose for ancient aid, as those who provide excellent sleep while seeking cattle. RV_04.041.07.2 We choose you for dear friendship—O heroes, most generous, bringing bliss like parents.

RV_04.041.08.1 These prayers of ours, seeking strength for your protection, have gone forth like racers toward you, O bounteous givers, longing for you both. RV_04.041.08.2 Like cows approaching the soma for its glory, my inspired thoughts have gone to Indra and Varuṇa.
RV_04.041.09.1 These inspired thoughts of mine, seeking wealth, have gone forth to Indra and Varuṇa.
They have approached like those who delight in wealth, like swift mares seeking a share of glory.
May we ourselves become masters of the abundance of horses and chariots, and of eternal riches. May they, performing deeds with their newest aids, attend us with yoked teams of wealth.
Come to us, O Great Ones, with your great aids, Indra and Varuṇa, in the struggle for booty.
When the flashing arrows play in the battles, may we be the winners of that prize through you both. Twofold is my sovereignty as a Kṣatriya, like all the immortals for Viśvāyu. As it is for us...
The gods follow the will of Varuṇa; I rule over the people, over the highest enclosure.
I am King Varuṇa; for me those first asuric powers were established. The gods follow the will of Varuṇa; I rule over the people, over the highest enclosure.
I am Indra and Varuṇa; by my greatness, I have established the two wide, deep, well-fashioned realms of space.
Like Tvaṣṭṛ, knowing all beings, I have brought together and sustained heaven and earth. I caused the waters to swell as they flowed, and I supported heaven in the seat of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).
By *ṛta*, the son of Aditi and upholder of *ṛta*, has spread out the earth in threefold measure.

Men with fine horses, seeking booty, call upon me when they are hemmed in by enemies in the clash of battle. I, Indra Maghavan, create the conflict; I stir up the dust, for my strength is overwhelming.
I have performed all these deeds; no divine power can restrain me, for my irresistible might is invincible.
When the Soma juices exhilarate me and when the hymns of praise [gladden] me, both the boundless realms tremble with fear.
You know all those worlds, O Ordainer; you proclaim them to Varuṇa.
You are renowned for having slain the Vṛtras; you, O Indra, set free the obstructed rivers.
Our fathers were here when the Seven Seers were being held captive by Durgaha. They offered sacrifice for Trasadasyu, who was half-divine, like Indra the subduer of Vṛtra.
For Purukutsānī has worshipped you both, O Indra and Varuṇa, with offerings and with prostrations.
Therefore, you two have given her King Trasadasyu, the slayer of Vṛtra, the demi-god.
May we, having won through wealth, rejoice, O gods, as cattle do through fodder and through the offering of oblations.
O Indra and Varuṇa, grant us every day that cow who never falters.
Who will hear? Which of the worshipful gods? Which god will take pleasure in our praise?
Whose heart shall we touch with this divine, most beloved hymn, well-offered among the immortals?
Who will show mercy? Which one is most ready to come? And which among the gods is the most beneficent?
Which chariot do they call swift with its racing horses—the one that the Daughter of the Sun chose? For you two indeed go quickly on such days, like Indra wielding his power in the decisive struggle.
Born from heaven, divine, fair-winged birds—by what power among powers do you become most powerful? What approach has been yours? By what means, O Aśvins, do you come to us when invoked?
Who, even from great abandonment, has brought you near? O bounteous ones, O wonder-workers, protect us with your aid!

Wide through the sky your chariot reaches, as it turns back from the ocean toward you both. O lovers of sweetness, with honey they sprinkle honey for you when they have cooked the nourishing foods for you.
Sindhu indeed sprinkles your horses with the Rasa; the ruddy birds have flown around, protected from the heat.
RV 4.43.6.2: Then indeed that swift vehicle of yours became known, by which you two became the lords of Sūryā.
RV 4.43.7.1: Since I have here and now gratified you both together, may this favor of yours, rich in booty, be ours.
RV 4.43.7.2: Protect the singer; for this desire of mine, O Nāsatyas, rests directed toward you.
O Aśvins, we invoke today that chariot of yours, which has broad tracks and brings the gathering of cattle;
it is the one that carries Sūryā, whose seat is full, which bears songs of praise, and which most frequently seeks out wealth.
O Aśvins, you two, the sons of Heaven, win that glory through your divine powers by means of your mighty deeds.
The nourishing foods attend upon your form when the towering steeds draw you in your chariot.
Who today, having offered oblations, will bring you with hymns for aid or for the drinking of the pressed juice?
Or who, offering homage, will turn you hither, O Aśvins, to favor the ancient lover of the Truth?
O Nāsatyas, you who exist in many places, come to this sacrifice on your golden chariot.
Drink of the honeyed Soma; bestow wealth upon the person who honors you.
Come to us from heaven and from earth on your well-rolling golden chariot.

RV_04.044.05.2 May other seekers of the gods not restrain you two, since our ancient kinship with you has been established. RV_04.044.06.1 Now, O wonder-workers, measure out for us great wealth consisting of many heroes among both of us.
RV_04.044.06.2 When the men who offered praise to you, O Aśvins, approached the joint hymn of praise, the Ājamīḷhas came forward.
RV_04.044.07.1 Here, here indeed, I have gratified you both together; may this benevolence of yours, rich in prizes, be with us.
RV_04.044.07.2 Protect the singer, for your desire, O Nāsatyas, rests directed toward you.

In this [soma] there are three nourishing draughts, joined in pairs; the fourth skin overflows with honey. Your nourishing draughts, rich in sweetness, rise up like chariots and horses at the dawning of the dawn.
Uncovering the darkness that enveloped it, they spread the bright light through the mid-air like the sun.
Drink of the honey with your honey-drinking mouths; moreover, harness your dear chariot for the sake of the honey.
You quicken the tracks and the paths with honey; O Aśvins, you carry a honey-filled skin.
Those swans of yours, full of honey, unerring, golden-winged, carrying you along, who wake at dawn—
Plunging into the waters, exhilarating and touching the exhilarating draughts, you two go to the libations like bees to honey.
The fires, well-sacrificing and rich in sweetness, sing at dawn toward the Aśvins at the break of day,
when the one with washed hands, the swift and far-seeing, has pressed the honeyed Soma with the stones.
With their mouths full of food, shaking off the darkness through the days, they spread the bright light across the mid-air like the sun.

Even as the Sun yokes his horses, you two travel; by your own power, you perceive all paths. O Aśvins, I, the inspirer of thought, have proclaimed your praise—the chariot that is yours, with its fine horses, which is ageless.

RV 4.45.7: By which [path] you traverse the regions instantly toward the one who possesses the oblation, the swift, the liberal giver. RV 4.46.1: Drink first of the pressed sweet juices, O Vāyu, at the sacrifices for heaven. RV 4.46.2: For you are the first to drink.
With a hundred aids, O Vāyu, whose charioteer is Indra, come with your team of horses; sate yourselves with the pressed juice. O Indra and Vāyu, a thousand bay steeds bring you toward the offerings.
May they carry you for the drinking of Soma—
Indra and Vāyu— to the chariot with its golden seat, which is well-adorned for the sacrifice, for you both occupy that which touches the heavens.
Come to the donor with your chariot of broad splendor;
O Indra and Vāyu, come here!
O Indra and Vāyu, this [Soma] has been pressed; [drink it] together with the gods in harmony.
Drink in the house of the donor.
May your journey here be for you, O Indra and Vāyu, and your unyoking; may it be here for you both to drink the Soma.
O Vāyu, the bright first portion of the honeyed mead is offered to you at the rites for the gods. Come, O desirable god, with your team of horses, to drink the Soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, you two are worthy of the drinking of these Somas.
For toward you two the drops flow together like waters descending to the lowlands.
O Vāyu and Indra, you two who are impetuous, lords of power, come on the same chariot with your teams of horses for our aid, to drink the Soma.
O Heroes, Indrā-Vāyu, those many-desired teams of yours which belong to the donor—bestow them upon us, you who bring the sacrifice.
Accept the invocations; like inspired songs, they are the wealth of the noble one.
O Vāyu, come with your radiant chariot to drink of the pressed soma.
Driving away all curses, accompanied by your teams of horses and with Indra as your charioteer—
O Vāyu, come with your radiant chariot to drink of the pressed soma.
The two dark treasuries of wealth, adorned with every ornament, have followed along.
O Vāyu, come on your shining chariot to drink of the pressed juice.
Let the ninety-nine horses, yoked by thought, carry you hither.
O Vāyu, come with your radiant chariot to drink of the pressed soma.
O Vāyu, harness a hundred well-fed bay horses;
or let your thousandfold chariot come hither with its full splendor.
This oblation is dear to you both from my mouth, O Indra and Bṛhaspati;
the hymn and the exhilarating draught are recited. This Soma is poured out for you both, O Indra and Bṛhaspati.
Charming for exhilaration and for drinking.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, come to our house; both of you, drinkers of Soma, come for the drinking of Soma.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, bestow upon us wealth consisting of hundreds,
consisting of horses, and consisting of thousands. O Indra and Bṛhaspati, we invoke you with songs when the soma is pressed.
For the drinking of this Soma.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, drink the Soma in the house of the donor; rejoice there, you who dwell together.

Bṛhaspati, who dwells in the three seats, has by his might and his roar propped apart the ends of the earth. The ancient seers, inspired and meditative, have placed him before them—him whose tongue is sweet. O Bṛhaspati, those who, like rushing winds, rejoicing and well-observing, have extended themselves toward us— RV_04.050.01.1 He who by his might has propped apart the ends of the earth, Bṛhaspati, dwelling in the three stations, with his roar;
RV_04.050.01.2 Him the ancient seers, meditating, the inspired ones, have placed in front, he whose tongue is sweet.
RV_04.050.02.1 O Bṛhaspati, those who, like rushing winds, rejoicing and well-observing, have extended themselves toward us—
O Bṛhaspati, protect the spotted, flowing, inviolable, wide expanse; guard the womb of this [sacrifice].
O Bṛhaspati, from that most distant distance, those who touch the cosmic order have sat down near you.
For you, the dug-out wells, milked by the stones, drip honey all around in abundance.
Bṛhaspati, being first born from the great light in the highest heaven,
seven-mouthed and many-born, blew away the darkness with his roar, he who has seven rays.
With his well-praising and hymn-singing host, he shattered Vala and Phaliga with his roar.
Bṛhaspati, bellowing loudly, drove forth the lowing ruddy cows that prepare the oblations.
Thus let us serve the father, the bull of all the gods, with sacrifices, homage, and offerings. O Bṛhaspati, may we, possessing good offspring and heroic sons, be masters of riches.

He indeed, as king, stands firm against all hostile forces by his might and through heroic deeds—he who maintains Bṛhaspati well-nourished, honors him, praises him, and offers him the first portion. He alone dwells securely in his own well-established home; for him, the sacrificial food flows abundantly at all times.
To that king the subjects bow down of their own accord, in whom the Brahman goes before. Unopposed, he conquers all treasures, both those of his enemies and those of his own kin.
The gods protect that king who grants freedom to the Brahman seeking his favor.

O Indra and Bṛhaspati, drink the Soma, rejoicing at this sacrifice, O you who possess bull-like wealth! May the self-sustaining drops enter you both; bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
O Bṛhaspati and Indra, cause us to prosper together; let that benevolence of yours be with us.
Favor our prayers; awaken our inspired thoughts; exhaust the hostilities of the enemy and of those who would attack us.
Yonder, that most abundant light, rich in discernment, has arisen from the darkness in the east.
Now indeed, O Dawns, daughters of Heaven, shining forth, create a path for the people.
The wondrous Dawns have stood in the east like sacrificial posts set up at the rites. Shining forth, the pure and purifying ones have flung open the doors of the enclosure of darkness.
Today, as they shine, may the wealthy Dawns awaken the liberal patrons for the sake of bestowing gifts.
Let the Paṇis sleep within the darkness, unseeing and unconscious in the midst of gloom. O Goddesses, will your journey today be ancient or new, O Uṣas’?
With that [light] by which you shone richly for Navagva, Aṅgira, Daśagva, and Saptāsya, O wealthy ones.
For you, O goddesses, with your horses that are harnessed by the *ṛta*, traverse all worlds in an instant.
Awakening the sleeping world, O Dawns—you who have two feet and four feet—rouse every living being to movement.
Where indeed was she, and which among them was the ancient one, by whose ordinance they fashioned the forms of the *ṛbhus*?
The auspiciousness which the radiant Dawns bring as they move is not to be distinguished, for they are alike, ageless, and true.
Truly, those blessed Dawns were of old, possessing the splendor of victory, born of *ṛta*, and true;
in them the sacrificer, striving with hymns, praising and reciting, immediately obtained wealth.
They come together from the east, spreading out from the same place;
awakening from the seat of Order, the goddesses Dawn break forth like herds of cattle.
Indeed, those Dawns, of uniform color, move together in the same manner.
Concealing their black terror with their radiant, bright bodies, pure and shining with light—
O divine daughters of heaven, as you shine forth, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny. As we awaken from your pleasant presence, may we be masters of heroic vigor.
O Dawns, daughters of heaven, shining forth, to you I speak as one whose banner is the sacrifice:
may we be glorious among the people; may Heaven and the Goddess Earth grant this.
The noble lady, shining forth, has appeared from her sister.
The daughter of heaven has been seen;
like a dappled mare, ruddy and true to the cosmic order, the mother of the cows,
Dawn, has become the friend of the Aśvins.
You are indeed the friend of the Aśvins, and you are the mother of the cows;
O Uṣas, you are the mistress of wealth.
O you who are rich in joy, may he who is observant take heed of you as one who drives away all enmity.
We have awakened with hymns of praise.
The auspicious rays have appeared like herds of cattle;
Dawn has filled the wide expanse.
O radiant one, having filled [the world], you have dispelled the darkness with your light;
O Uṣas, favor us according to your own nature.
You extend across the sky with your rays, and across the wide, beloved intermediate space.
O Uṣas, with your bright radiance!
We choose that great and desirable gift of the divine Savitṛ, the wise Asura, by which he himself bestows protection upon the donor; may that Great God extend it to us through the nights.
The upholder of heaven, Prajāpati of the world, the sage, puts on his tawny mantle.
Far-seeing, spreading abroad and filling the wide space, Savitar has generated praiseworthy bliss. He has reached the celestial and earthly regions; the god makes his proclamation for his own law.
Savitar has stretched out his arms to impel the world; laying it to rest and setting it in motion by means of the nights.

Unassailable, surveying all beings, the god Savitar protects the sacred laws. He has stretched out his arms for the sake of the creatures of the world; firm in his vows, he rules over the great course of the universe.
Savitar thrice traverses the mid-air by his greatness; he encompasses the three regions and the three luminous spheres.
He impels the three heavens and the three earths; with his three ordinances, he protects us by his own self.
He who possesses lofty bliss, the impeller, the one who brings rest, the lord of both that which moves and that which stands—him [we praise].
May that god Savitṛ grant us protection, a triple-shielded refuge for our dwelling against distress.

The god has come with the seasons; may he cause our dwelling to prosper. May Savitṛ bestow upon us food accompanied by good progeny. May he quicken us through nights and days; may he bring together for us wealth consisting of offspring.

The god Savitar has become worthy of praise for us; he is now to be invoked by men at this time of day, he who distributes treasures to human beings so that he may grant us the most excellent wealth here. For you first bestow immortality as the supreme portion upon the gods who are worthy of sacrifice.
Then, O Savitṛ, you have indeed spread out the gift, bestowing successive lives upon human beings.
Whatever we have done through lack of insight among the divine folk— with feeble intellects, through our own human nature—
O Savitṛ, among both gods and men, do you here grant us freedom from sin.
That power of the divine Savitṛ is not to be measured, by which he shall sustain the entire world.
Whatever the one with beautiful fingers brings forth upon the breadth of the earth and the height of heaven—that is his truth.
To these great mountains, you, whose lord is Indra, ordain dwellings provided with houses.

Just as they spread themselves out while flying, so indeed have they stood still for your impulsion, O Savitṛ. O Savitṛ, those impulses of yours which three times a day, day after day, bring us prosperity—
May Indra, Heaven and Earth, Sindhu with her waters, and Aditi with the Ādityas, grant us protection.

The ordainers have established you; the unwearied ones, whose thoughts are fixed on the *ṛta*, have shone forth as wonder-workers.
With hymns, I invoke for friendship the goddess Aditi, the mistress of the house, and the Sindhu river, and Svasti.
May both Uṣas and Night, the undeceivable ones, protect us through the day and night.
Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Agni, the lord of nourishment, have made the path clear—the way to prosperity.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, being well praised, grant us manly protection and powerful shelter.
I have invoked the aids of Parvata, of the Maruts, and of the divine savior Bhaga.
May the Lord protect us from the distress caused by strangers, and may Mitra deliver us from the hostility of those who seek alliance.
Now let the two goddesses, Heaven and Earth, be praised along with Ahi Budhnya by these desired offerings of water;
like those seeking gain at the gathering place, the rivers, resonant with the heat of the sun, have opened their channels toward the ocean.
May the goddess Aditi protect us with the gods; may the god, the Savior, protect us without ceasing. For we do not deserve to diminish the nourishment of Mitra and Varuṇa upon the back of Agni.
Agni is the lord of wealth; Agni is the lord of great fortune.
May she grant those things to us. O bountiful Dawn, O giver of joy, bring hither many desirable gifts for us, O lady rich in spoils.
May Savitṛ, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,
and Indra come to us with bounty.
May the great Heaven and Earth, the two eldest, be present here with splendor and with radiant hymns.

When he, the bull, roars while fashioning that which is most wide and vast, with his far-reaching movements; then the two goddesses, worthy of sacrifice, worshipful among the gods, standing undecaying and swelling,
abide there— truthful, guileless, daughters of the gods, leaders of the sacrifice with their radiant hymns.

He indeed was the skillful craftsman among the worlds, he who brought these two, heaven and earth, into being; the wise one, by his power, has established the two wide, deep, well-measured, and firmly fixed realms in the supportless space.
Now may Rodasī, together with their consorts, providing nourishment and acting in harmony, protect us with their vast defenses.
O wide-reaching, universal, and worshipful ones, protect us; through our prayer, may we be chariot-borne victors forever.
We bring forth our great hymn of praise unto you two, O Heaven and Earth, pure ones, for the sake of exaltation.
Purifying each other’s bodies, you rule by your own inherent skill;
from of old, you have been carried as the Eternal Order (*ṛta*). O Great Ones, you accomplish the purpose of Mitra, crossing over and fulfilling the Eternal Order.
You two have taken your seats around the sacrifice.
Through the Lord of the Field, as if with a well-placed ally, may we win;
may he who nourishes cattle and horses be gracious toward us such as we are.
O Lord of the Field, pour out for us a honeyed wave, as a cow yields her milk;
may the lords of the Eternal Law (Ṛta) be gracious to us—[a wave] dripping with honey, well-purified like clarified butter.
May the plants be full of sweetness, may the heavens and the waters [be so]; may the mid-air be sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Field be full of sweetness for us; may we follow him without injury.
Prosperity to the draft-animals! Prosperity to the men! May the plough furrow with prosperity.
May the leather thongs be bound with prosperity; may you lift the goad with prosperity.
O Śuna and Sīra, may you both take pleasure in this speech; with that milk which you created in heaven, sprinkle upon this earth.
O auspicious furrow, turn toward us; we revere you, O Sītā.
So that you may be auspicious for us, so that you may bear good fruit for us—may Indra take hold of the furrow; may Pūṣan follow it.
May she, rich in milk, yield her bounty for us year after year.
May our ploughshares furrow the earth auspiciously; may the plowmen go forth auspiciously with their draft-animals.
May Parjanya bless us with honeyed milk; O Śunāsīras, bestow prosperity upon us!
From the ocean the honeyed wave has risen; through the *upāṃśu* cup, it has attained immortality.

That which is the secret name of clarified butter is the tongue of the gods and the navel of immortality. Let us proclaim the name of clarified butter; let us uphold it with our homages at this sacrifice.
May the Brahman hear the recitation being performed; the four-horned bull has bellowed this.
Four are his horns, three are his feet, two are his heads, and seven are his hands.
Bound in three places, the bull bellows loudly; the great god has entered into mortals.
The gods discovered the clarified butter (ghṛta) hidden by the Paṇis, established in three ways within the cow.
Indra begot one, Sūrya begot one; from Vena they fashioned one by their own inherent power.
These [streams] flow from the ocean within the heart, with a hundred enclosures, not to be seen by the enemy.
I gaze upon the streams of clarified butter; golden is the reed in their midst.
The streams flow forth together like rivers, being purified within by the heart and the mind.
These waves of clarified butter rush onward like deer fleeing from a swift hunter.
Like the rapid currents of a river on its course, they fly forth, mighty and overtaking the wind.
The streams of clarified butter flow like a ruddy steed, bursting through the barriers and swelling with its waves.
Like beautiful women smiling as they go to a gathering, the streams of clarified butter have approached Agni.
These streams of ghee reach the fuel-wood; finding them pleasing, Jātavedas accepts them with delight.
Like maidens anointing themselves for the wedding procession, I gaze upon the ointments being applied.
Where Soma is pressed and where the sacrifice is performed, there the streams of clarified butter flow pure.
Flow toward our excellent praise; bestow upon us the wealth of cattle and auspicious riches.
Lead this sacrifice of ours to the gods; the streams of clarified butter flow sweetly.
Upon your abode the entire world is supported—within the ocean, within the heart, and within life.
May we attain that honeyed wave of yours, which has been brought forth at the meeting-place on the surface of the waters.
